title: Cloud Connector Insights pages and Insights logs: time range, aggregation and limits

prose.text: The Insights pages chart connector traffic, and each has a Logs tab with the underlying records. Their limits shape what an investigation in the console can show.

prose.label: Charts.
prose.text: {{units}} {{time-frame}} {{top-n}} How per-day aggregation treats day boundaries is open {{gap:multi-day-aggregation}}.

prose.label: Logs pages.
prose.text: {{insights-logs-pages}} How far back a query can start, against the 180-day storage in [[cloud-connector.logs:nanolog-180]], is open {{gap:query-range-vs-retention}}. A programmatic read of these logs is open {{gap:insights-log-api}}.

prose.label: Tunnel Insights.
prose.text: {{tunnel-data-types}} {{tunnel-bytes-perspective}} Whether these byte counts match the session records for the same traffic is open {{gap:byte-count-parity}}. Whether a chart can be narrowed to one connector VM is open {{gap:tunnel-per-connector}}, and what a fall in DPD Received means is open {{gap:dpd-semantics}}.

prose.label: Session Insights filters.
prose.text: {{session-data-types}} {{session-filters}} The Traffic Direction filter's definition is cut off in the capture {{gap:traffic-direction-definition}}. {{session-log-filters}}

prose.label: Freshness.
prose.text: How soon a transaction appears in Insights is open {{gap:insights-latency}}.

checks.do: Whether the chart spans several days, in which case values are per-day sums and an intraday spike is hidden; narrow to one day.
Whether a trend or pie chart is hiding the item of interest in Other, since those charts show only the top 5.
Which side a tunnel byte count is measured from before comparing it with workload-side numbers.

units.statement: Session Insights is measured in Sessions or Bytes, DNS Insights in Transactions, and Tunnel Insights in DPD Received, Received Bytes, Received Packets, Sent Bytes and Sent Packets.

quotes: Session Insights: Sessions, Bytes
DNS Insights: Transactions
Tunnel Insights: DPD Received, Received Bytes, Received Packets, Sent Bytes, and Sent Packets

time-frame.statement: A custom time frame can end up to 92 days after its start date, and selecting multiple days shows the sum of bytes or transactions per day in whichever chart type is selected.

quotes: In Custom, the end date can be up to 92 days after the start date. Selecting multiple days results in seeing the sum of bytes/transactions per day in whichever chart type you select.

top-n.statement: For certain data types the chart can show the top 5, 10, 25, 50 or 100 items; trend and pie charts show only the top 5, with the rest grouped as Other.

quotes: For certain data types, you can choose to view the top 5, 10, 25, 50, or 100 items.
In trend and pie charts, you'll only see the top 5 items. The "Other" category refers to the rest of the data types that are not in the top 5.

drilldown.statement: Filters, some of which take multiple values, are applied with Apply Filters; hovering on a chart item and selecting Click for more info opens the logs for it.

quotes: Select filters. Certain filters support the selection of multiple values.
Click Apply Filters to activate your changes.
View logs for a specific item in the chart. Hover and click it, and then select Click for more info to view the Logs.

history-bar.statement: The history bar keeps up to 50 versions of the chart, deleting the oldest beyond that; changing an earlier version deletes all versions after it.

quotes: The history bar can retain up to 50 versions of the chart. If there are more than 50 versions, the Zscaler Admin Console deletes the oldest versions as new ones are added.
If you view an earlier version and change it, all subsequent versions are automatically deleted.

insights-logs-pages.statement: Each Insights page has a Logs tab (the Session, DNS and Tunnel logs pages) with filters, a custom time frame ending up to 92 days after its start, a choice of Display or Download, and selectable columns; downloads are in the time zone set on the My Profile page.

quotes: You can view the following logs pages:
Session Logs
DNS Logs
Tunnel Logs
Choose the Logs tab, located at the top left corner of each Insights page.
In Custom, the end date can be up to 92 days after the start date.
Select Display to view logs, or select Download to download logs. Logs are downloaded in the time zone set on the My Profile page.
Customize your log view by selecting or deselecting which column fields you want to see.

tunnel-data-types.statement: Besides Overall Traffic, a Tunnel Insights chart can break traffic down by Location, Tunnel Destination IP and Tunnel Source IP, and filters such as Location narrow it.

quotes: The following Tunnel Insights instance is used to walk you through how to use the Insights pages. It shows a trend chart for the data type Overall Traffic.
Other data type options include Location, Tunnel Destination IP, and Tunnel Source IP.
Under Select Filters, select Location to filter accordingly.

session-data-types.statement: Session Insights can be viewed by the data types Overall Traffic, Traffic Direction, TS Direction (traffic stream direction), Traffic Type, Connector Instance, Connector Group, Azure Subscription ID, Platform, Forwarding Rule, Forwarding Type and Location.

quotes: You can view the Session Insights based on the following data types:
- TS Direction (traffic stream direction)
- Connector Instance
- Connector Group

evidence.after: You can view the Session Insights based on the following data types:
quotes: - Overall Traffic
- Traffic Direction
- Traffic Type
- Azure Subscription ID
- Platform
- Forwarding Rule
- Forwarding Type
- Location

session-filters.statement: Session Insights filters include AWS Availability Zone (the zone where Cloud Connector for AWS is deployed), CC VM (traffic of one Cloud Connector VM), Cloud Connector Instance (the specific Zscaler software instance), Platform (the hypervisor or cloud platform), TS Direction (transmitted TX or received RX traffic) and Traffic Type (ZIA, ZPA or direct).

quotes: AWS Availability Zone: Limits the data to traffic associated with the availability zone where Cloud Connector for AWS is deployed.
CC VM: Limits the data to traffic associated with the Cloud Connector virtual machine (VM) from which you want to view the session insights.
Cloud Connector Instance: Limits the data to traffic associated with the specific Zscaler software instance.
Platform: Limits the data to traffic associated with the hypervisor or the cloud platform from which you want to see the session insights.
TS Direction: Limits the data to either transmitted (TX) or received (RX) traffic.
Traffic Type: Limits the data to traffic associated with the type of traffic: ZIA, ZPA, or direct.

tunnel-chart-filters.statement: Tunnel Insights chart filters include Location (the default is All; the filter lists 200 results at a time with search fields), Tunnel Destination IP and Tunnel Source IP.

quotes: You can use tunnel data types and filters to define the tunnel traffic information that you want to view when analyzing charts on an Insights page.
Location: Use this filter to view metrics associated with a specific location. The default option for this filter is All.
The Location filter lists 200 results at a time. It provides search fields where you can enter characters and narrow the results to match your input.
Tunnel Destination IP: Use this filter to view metrics associated with a destination IP address.
Tunnel Source IP: Use this filter to view metrics associated with a source IP address.

tunnel-log-filters.statement: The Tunnel Insights logs filters include a Data Center filter, and the Tunnel Destination IP and Tunnel Source IP filters can each take a range of IP addresses (for example 192.0.2.0-192.0.2.100) or a subnet mask (for example 192.0.2.0/24) when filtering by multiple IP addresses.

quotes: Data Center: Use this filter to view metrics associated with a specific data center.

evidence.after: - Tunnel Destination IP: Use this filter to view metrics associated with a destination IP address. If you want to filter by multiple IP addresses, you can enter:
quotes: A range of IP addresses (e.g., 192.0.2.0-192.0.2.100).
A subnet mask (e.g., 192.0.2.0/24).

evidence.after: - Tunnel Source IP: Use this filter to view metrics associated with a source IP address. If you want to filter by multiple IP addresses, you can enter:
quotes: A range of IP addresses (e.g., 192.0.2.0-192.0.2.100).
A subnet mask (e.g., 192.0.2.0/24).

session-log-filters.statement: Session Insights logs filters include Application Segment, Client Destination Name (for Advanced Firewall, a specific destination FQDN), Cloud Connector Source Port (the source port of the Cloud Connector used to connect to the forwarding gateway), Gateway Name, Network Service and Server Source Port.

quotes: Application Segment: Use this filter to view transactions associated with a specific application segment.
Client Destination Name: For Advanced Firewall, use this filter to limit the data to traffic associated with a specific destination FQDN.
Cloud Connector Source Port: Use this filter to limit the data to traffic associated with the source port of the Cloud Connector that is used to connect to the forwarding gateway.
Gateway Name: Use this filter to limit the data to traffic associated with the gateway name used.
Network Service: The network service associated with the session or aggregated sessions.
Server Source Port: Use this filter to limit the data to traffic associated with a specific server source port.

dns-log-filters.statement: DNS Insights logs filters include DNS Gateway Flag, DNS Rule Name (the rule triggered by the DNS request, response or both), Protocol Type (TCP or UDP), Request Action (the action the DNS Control policy took), and a Requested Domain filter taking Contains, Starts With, Ends With, Exact Match, Does Not Contain, Does Not End With, Not Null or Is Null; locations can be included or excluded.

quotes: DNS Gateway Flag: Use this filter to limit the data to traffic associated with the DNS gateway flag.
DNS Rule Name: The rule that was triggered by the DNS request, response, or both.
Protocol Type: Use this filter to limit data to either TCP or UDP traffic.
Request Action: Use this filter to limit the data to a specific action that your DNS Control policy took.
Requested Domain: Use this filter to limit the data to the traffic associated with the domain for which DNS resolution was requested.
Enter all or part of the domain in the text field and choose Contains, Starts With, Ends With, Exact Match, Does Not Contain, Does Not End With, Not Null, or Is Null.
You can choose to include or exclude certain locations.

dns-bytes.statement: In the DNS Insights logs, the In Bytes filter limits the data to packets sent from the server to the client within a specific size range, and Out Bytes to packets the server received within a specific size range.

quotes: In Bytes: Use this filter to limit the data to packets sent from the server to the client that were within a specific size range.
Out Bytes: Use this filter to limit the data to packets that the server received that were within a specific size range.

tunnel-bytes-perspective.statement: Tunnel log byte and packet counts are taken from Zscaler's side over a one-minute sample interval: Bytes Received and Packets Received are what Zscaler received through the tunnel from the organization, and Bytes Sent and Packets Sent what Zscaler sent through the tunnel to the organization.

quotes: Bytes Received: The total bytes of data Zscaler received through the tunnel from the organization in the one-minute sample interval.
Bytes Sent: The total bytes of data Zscaler sent through the tunnel to the organization in the one-minute sample interval.
Packets Received: The total number of packets Zscaler received through the tunnel from the organization in the one-minute sample interval.
Packets Sent: The total number of packets Zscaler sent through the tunnel to the organization in the one-minute sample interval.

traffic-direction-definition.title: What the Traffic Direction filter limits the data to
traffic-direction-definition.detail: The Session Insights filter list gives the Traffic Direction filter as limiting the data to traffic associated with, and the capture breaks off there. DNS Gateway Flag and the Endpoint and Interface values are also not defined.

quotes: Traffic Direction: Limits the data to traffic associated with

byte-count-parity.title: Whether Tunnel Insights byte counts match session-record byte counts for the same traffic
byte-count-parity.blocks: reconciling tunnel throughput with per-session volumes
byte-count-parity.detail: Whether Tunnel Insights byte counts match the byte counts of session records for the same sessions is unverified, and whether the chart units Received Bytes and Sent Bytes use the Zscaler-side perspective of the tunnel log columns (claim tunnel-bytes-perspective) is not stated; the legacy page described Received Bytes as bytes received by the connector. Ledger cloud-connector-21 also held the Insights download API (gap insights-log-api) and multi-day aggregation (gap multi-day-aggregation).

insights-log-api.title: Whether Insights logs can be read through an API
insights-log-api.blocks: automating the export of connector Insights logs without an NSS feed
insights-log-api.detail: The console's Logs tab offers a Download (claim insights-logs-pages), and no API path for Insights is in the captured reference (cloud-connector.insights:no-insights-api). An undocumented or newer API endpoint is not excluded. Former cloud-connector-21 item 1.

multi-day-aggregation.title: How multi-day Insights charts aggregate per day
multi-day-aggregation.blocks: comparing per-day Insights values with SIEM counts bucketed in another time zone
multi-day-aggregation.detail: The help states that multiple days show the sum of bytes or transactions per day (claim time-frame); which time zone sets the day boundary, and how Sessions and Tunnel packet units aggregate, is not stated. Former cloud-connector-21 item 3.

query-range-vs-retention.title: How far back an Insights query can start
query-range-vs-retention.blocks: deciding whether the console can answer a question about traffic more than a few months old
query-range-vs-retention.detail: Unverified legacy statement (open question): whether Insights retention is the 92-day maximum window or shorter. Logs are stored for 180 days and a custom window spans up to 92 days; whether the start date can be set anywhere in the 180 days is not stated.

insights-latency.title: Delay between a transaction and its appearance in Insights
insights-latency.blocks: deciding during an incident whether missing Insights data is a delay or a real absence
insights-latency.detail: No captured source states how long after a session ends it appears in Session Insights or its logs.

tunnel-per-connector.title: Whether Tunnel Insights can be narrowed to one connector VM
tunnel-per-connector.blocks: isolating one failing connector's tunnel statistics
tunnel-per-connector.detail: The documented Tunnel Insights data types are Overall Traffic, Location, Tunnel Destination IP and Tunnel Source IP (claim tunnel-data-types), and the Tunnel logs have a Cloud Connector Instance column; whether the chart can be filtered to one VM or only to a location or tunnel IP is not stated. The Tunnel chart filters page lists Location, Tunnel Destination IP and Tunnel Source IP (claim tunnel-chart-filters) and no per-connector filter, an absence read from that page.

quotes: Cloud Connector Instance: The specific Zscaler software instance

dpd-semantics.title: What a drop in DPD Received means
dpd-semantics.blocks: telling an upstream tunnel fault from a connector fault in Tunnel Insights
dpd-semantics.detail: Unverified legacy statement: DPD Received counts "Dead Peer Detection keepalive packets received from the ZIA/ZPA peer — proxy for tunnel liveness". The help names DPD Received as a unit and does not define it.
